summary: Offering the carried, not-yet-known fake Amulet on a low altar reaches pray.c:offer_fake_amulet, but js/pray.js stops at note_unported. In this aligned neutral case C calls offer_too_soon and displays “You feel an urge to return to the surface.” Port the whole fake-Amulet helper and that feedback helper, then replace the dosacrifice placeholder with the helper call.

source.branch: In dosacrifice, the selected object is FAKE_AMULET_OF_YENDOR; highaltar is false and otmp->known is false. offer_fake_amulet therefore calls offer_too_soon and returns before the thunderclap/known-Amulet branches. For an aligned, non-hallucinating hero, offer_too_soon displays the urge-to-return message.
callers: cmd.c:rhack/doextcmd (outer extended-command input path reaches the "offer" entry mapped to dosacrifice; this generic dispatcher already routes the selected command).
cmd.c:ext command table entry "offer" maps #offer to dosacrifice
js/cmd.js:MCMD.OFFER queues dosacrifice; runCommand("dosacrifice") dispatches to js/pray.js:dosacrifice
dependencies: pray.c:offer_too_soon is the direct missing callee for the observed low-altar/unknown-object branch and belongs in the same source task.
pray.c:offer_negative_valued is called by offer_fake_amulet for a known fake Amulet and already has a JavaScript implementation in js/pray.js; its existing desecrate_altar gap remains at that callee.

pray.c:gods_upset is called by offer_too_soon for an unaligned altar in Gehennom and already has a JavaScript implementation; message, sound, luck, and alignment operations used by other offer_fake_amulet branches are existing game APIs.

evidence: C source: nethack-c/upstream/src/pray.c:1601-1627 makes offer_fake_amulet call offer_too_soon and return when !highaltar && !otmp->known; nethack-c/upstream/src/pray.c:1477-1498 selects “an urge to return to the surface” when altar alignment matches the hero and Hallucination is false. This is the exact branch represented by the recorded final screen.
